scope: Squarefree differences between actual odd primes: the uniform global signed spectrum, positive Euler-product density, asymptotically optimal density1/2 and quantitative parity rigidity are kernel checked. Optimality of the residual spectral factor1/5 remains pending in SFS-SHARP.

claims.claim: A single constant bounds every nonprincipal prime-character prefix by C*X^(7/8)*(1+log m+log(X+2))^2.

One C>0 uniformly bounds primeSquareTailCount(p,X,R) by pi(X)/R+C*T*X^(7/8)*(1+log(T^2)+log(X+2))^2+2*floor(X/T), for every prime p<=X and 2<=R<=T. The count excludes q=p and uses congruence modulo a prime square ell^2 with ell>R.
claims.proof_scope: Complete finite bound, including nonunit exceptional row, both difference directions and every high divisor; its normalized limit is checked separately in SFS-TAIL-LIMIT.

claims.claim: Every algebraically generated finite product of normalized complete graphs with factor sizes at least six has centered quadratic gap at most 1/5, for every real function. The binary extension retains total-mean and parity-mean modes with the same residual bound. The zero-one product has an explicit positive density, and its full binary extension satisfies the exact unnormalized model hypothesis of the finite-fibre transfer.
claims.new_content: Classical finite product spectral calculation, supporting the admitted prime transfer.
claims.ordinary_spectral_description: The finite product of unit-residue inequality kernels has modes indexed by coordinate subsets, eigenvalues D_R*product(-1/(ell*(ell-1)-1)), and residual norm D_R/5 after constant and parity modes are removed.
claims.formal_scope: Normalized finite-product induction and the zero-one density conversion with binary parity, uniformly over every real function. The construction hypotheses carry finite graph data and cardinality conditions, with no analytic estimate. The concrete dependent function carrier is now constructed algebraically and satisfies the exact unnormalized binary gap, including the empty index type.
pending_adapters: Full eigenvalue formula (7), if required as a separately formalized classification

claims.claim: For every finite indexed family of odd primes, including repetitions and the empty family, the actual prime-square unit-residue inequality kernel with one binary coordinate has density D=(1/2)*product(1-1/(ell*(ell-1))) and the exact signed two-mode gap D/5 for every real function. Units modulo four are explicitly identified with Bool, preserving residue equality, parity sign and the inverse residue decoder.
claims.proof_scope: Concrete finite model and three modulo-four identities. The actual regular-prime map and complete finite consumer are checked in SFS-PRIME-FINITE; the asymptotic transfer is checked in SFS-FIBRE.
claims.new_content: Supporting finite arithmetic specialization of the classical product gap; not an independent novelty claim.

claims.claim: For every finite support, every real test function, a two-mode model gap and upper occupancy M*#fibre<=(1+delta)*n transfer to the full signed kernel with error (D*delta/5+(4*D+2)*tau+tau^2)*energy, when the exceptional support has size at most tau^2*n. Both exceptional cross orientations, the exceptional self interaction, and both squared principal means are included.
claims.proof_scope: Full finite transfer and complete exception treatment. Its application to the actual prime residue product is checked in SFS-PRIME-FINITE and its limit in SFS-FIBRE.

claims.claim: For every finite set S of primes, local prime-square congruence equality implies equality modulo their full product; primes outside S are units modulo that product; phi(product p^2)=product p*(p-1), equal to the cardinality of the full dependent unit-tuple space. The empty product and prime two are included.
claims.new_content: Classical arithmetic inputs supporting the admitted prime-spectrum transfer; not independent novelty claims.

claims.claim: One positive constant precedes every modulus, endpoint, finite regular-prime set, fibre type and map: each fibre is at most pi(X)/phi(N)+C*X^(7/8)*(1+log N+log(X+2))^2, provided the set consists of unit primes and equality of fibre labels implies congruence modulo N. Empty fibres and modulus one are included. The actual residue tuple of every prime outside a finite coordinate-prime set S satisfies this bound, with N=product(p^2), M=product(p*(p-1))=phi(N), and the same constant before S, X and every tuple label.
claims.new_content: Supporting arithmetic corollary of the existing uniform reduced-residue estimate; not an independently claimed novel result.
claims.exceptional_primes: The regular set is exactly primes at most X outside S; this includes the empty coordinate set and the coordinate prime two.

claims.claim: One C>0 precedes every finite set S of odd primes, endpoint X with n>0 odd primes, tau>=0 with |S|<=tau^2*n, and real weight f. For the actual cutoff kernel K_S, abs(q_S-D*(a^2-b^2))<=D/5*(e-a^2-b^2)+(D*delta/5+(4*D+2)*tau+tau^2)*e, where delta=(1+M*C*X^(7/8)*(1+log N+log(X+2))^2)/n, N=product_{p in insert 2 S}(p^2), M=product_{p in insert 2 S}(p*(p-1)), and D=(1/2)*product_{p in S}(1-1/(p*(p-1))).
claims.proof_scope: Actual odd-prime vertices, all signed real weights, empty coordinate set, prime-two center correction and all coordinate-prime exceptions. The asymptotic limit is SFS-FIBRE; stability is SFS-STABILITY; optimality remains pending in SFS-SHARP.

claims.claim: For every fixed finite set S of odd primes and eps>0, eventually for every X and every signed real weight f, abs(q_S-D*(a^2-b^2))<=D/5*(e-a^2-b^2)+eps*e. The eventual cutoff is independent of f; empty S and all coordinate-prime exceptions are included.
claims.proof_scope: Uses the existing unconditional prime-counting theorem to prove X^rho*(A+log(X+2))^k/n_X -> 0 for every fixed rho<1, A>=0 and k>=0. Takes tau_X=sqrt(|S|/n_X) and lets the complete finite error tend to zero before introducing f. No growing-modulus estimate, full squarefree tail, optimality or inverse consequence is asserted.

claims.claim: For every fixed R>=2 and eps>0, eventually uniformly over every prime p<=X, H_R,X(p)/n_X<=1/R+eps. Uniformly over every real weight f, the physical squarefree-gap quadratic form differs from its finite-cutoff form by at most (1/R+eps)*mean(f^2), and abs(Q_X-D_R*(a^2-b^2))<=D_R/5*(e-a^2-b^2)+(1/R+eps)*e.
claims.kernel_definition: PrimeFactorOscillations.QRH.primeSquarefreeDifferenceKernel p q is 1 exactly when Squarefree (((q:Int)-(p:Int)).natAbs), and 0 otherwise.
claims.quantitative_scope: One C>0 works for all R>=2, X>=(R+2)^16 and prime p<=X: H<=pi(X)/R+9*C*X^(15/16)*(1+log(X+2))^2+4*X^(15/16). The normalized cutoffs are uniform over both the moving prime and all signed weights.
claims.proof_scope: Both source errors, every exceptional finite interaction and both signed principal means are retained. A row estimate is applied only to the separated nonnegative symmetric tail. The infinite Euler-product density is checked in SFS-SPECTRAL and parity rigidity in SFS-STABILITY; optimality remains pending in SFS-SHARP.

claims.claim: For the explicitly defined unconditional Euler-product constant A with 1/4<=A<=1/2, for every eps>0 eventually uniformly over every real weight on the odd primes<=X, abs(Q_X-A*(a^2-b^2))<=A/5*(e-a^2-b^2)+eps*e.
claims.constant_definition: artinPrimeSquareConstant is inf_R primeSquareCutoffDensity R. HasProd proves it equals the unconditional Euler product with factor 1-1/(p*(p-1)) at every prime and factor 1 at nonprimes.
claims.proof_scope: All signed real weights, the actual Squarefree absolute-gap kernel, both principal means and the entire residual. The coefficient replacement keeps its exact correction and costs at most (6/5)*(D_R-A)*e; R is chosen before X and f. Parity rigidity is checked separately in SFS-STABILITY; optimality remains pending in SFS-SHARP.

claims.claim: A mean-zero unit-residue function modulo9 attains limiting Rayleigh quotient -A/5, so the residual factor1/5 is optimal.

For every eps>0 eventually uniformly over all squarefree-difference-free B contained in the actual odd primes<=X, 6*alpha^2-4*beta^2<=alpha+eps, alpha<=1/2+eps, and the normalized distance to the nearer residue class1 or3 modulo4 is at most1/2-sqrt(max(0,6*alpha^2-alpha))/2+eps. Both classes are independent and their relative densities tend to1/2.
claims.proof_scope: Every actual prime subset after one eps-dependent threshold; exact finite parity imbalance and both symmetric-difference identities retained. The proof consumes SFS-SPECTRAL and A>=1/4 without a new character estimate. Sharpness of density1/2 is proved; optimality of the spectral factor1/5 is not claimed.
